prompt: Storybook painterly illustration, night, HIGH CONTRAST with deep true blacks. A MINIATURE VILLAGE BUILT BY CAT-SIZED CREATURES — the whole settlement is tiny, and its scale is shown by NATURE TOWERING OVER IT: fern fronds arch higher than the rooflines, blades of grass rise past the eaves, a fallen pine cone beside the lane is larger than a barrel, mushroom caps stand as tall as the doorways, moss grows like shrubbery, dewdrops are heavy and huge on the leaves. The buildings are small and beautifully made: charred black cedar siding, fresh pale milled timber, tiny corrugated roofs, deep eaves, dry-stacked pebble footings, small salvaged glass windows. LIMITED NIGHT PALETTE: near-black, deep indigo, slate, moss green; the ONLY saturated colour is warm amber light from the windows. No text, no lettering, no signage. Close view at ground level: a single tiny dwelling among towering grass and fern, its small window glowing warm. In the lit window sits ONE CREATURE AS A PERFECT BLACK SILHOUETTE — completely featureless, defined only by its rounded shape, upright posture and the curl of a tail, holding up a single trading card that is nearly as tall as it is, examining it against the lamplight so the card face glows in its hands. A moth-sized moment. Everything else is dark: wet leaves, dripping fern, a pebble step, one fallen seed pod.
